short: AV-HuBERT's masked audio-visual cluster pre-training (M03) was a large step past distillation, but its LRS3 gains lack repeated runs and later work beats it at matched budgets.
position: The paper [@shi2022avhubert] changes two components: the pre-training objective (M03), masked prediction of audio-visual cluster labels refined over five iterations, and audio as training-only supervision (M02), with video alone at test. The M03 gain is large on the paper's own terms: its scratch baseline falls from 92.3% to 32.5% WER at 30 h of labels, and it is far below the 59.8% of cross-modal distillation [@afouras2020asr], although that margin also mixes 334 h against 1,759 h of unlabelled video. Both components remain standard by our rules, because the effect is shown on one test set with no repeated runs in Table 1. Later work now beats the design at the same budget: 23.7% against 32.5% with the same model size, unlabelled data and 30 h of labels [@haliassos2026usr2] [later]. The headline claim of beating the best prior system with 1/1000 of the labels overreaches: 32.5% against 33.6% [@makino2019rnnt] is a 1.1-point gap between different training regimes with no variance reported.
